mbr.badge: Regulated by Ministry of Health Malaysia
mbr.subtitle: Surgical Correction of Enlarged Male Chest (Gynecomastia)
mbr.heroDesc1: Male breast reduction is a surgical procedure designed to treat enlarged male breasts caused by glandular tissue, excess fat, or a combination of both. The goal is to create a flatter, firmer, and more masculine chest contour.
mbr.heroDesc2: In Malaysia, male breast reduction surgery must be performed in licensed medical facilities under the oversight of the Ministry of Health Malaysia, ensuring patient safety and regulated surgical standards.
mbr.whatIsDesc: Male breast reduction is a surgical treatment for gynecomastia, a condition involving abnormal enlargement of male breast tissue. The procedure removes excess glandular tissue, fat, and sometimes loose skin to restore normal chest proportions.
mbr.mayoNote: According to the Mayo Clinic, gynecomastia often does not resolve without surgery when firm glandular tissue is present.

mbr.faqDesc: Get answers to common concerns about male breast reduction
mbr.faq0Q: What is male breast reduction surgery?
mbr.faq0A: It is a surgical procedure to remove excess fat and glandular tissue from the male chest.
mbr.faq1Q: Is male breast reduction the same as gynecomastia surgery?
mbr.faq1A: Yes. Male breast reduction is the surgical treatment for gynecomastia.
mbr.faq2A: Yes. Removed glandular tissue does not grow back.
mbr.faq3A: Scars are minimal and usually hidden around the areola.
mbr.faq4A: Most patients return to work within 7–10 days.
mbr.faq5A: Exercise may reduce fat but cannot remove glandular tissue.
mbr.faq6A: Pain is typically mild to moderate and well controlled with medication.
mbr.faq7A: Yes, when performed by a qualified plastic surgeon in a regulated facility.
